question: Vortex generators on a wing upper surface delay separation by:

options.text: Shedding streamwise vortices that mix high-energy outer air into the near-wall layer
Removing the boundary layer by suction
Reducing the angle of attack locally, which lowers the lift on the wing surface in front of the generators and so keeps the flow attached to the upper surface
Reducing the angle of attack locally

explanation: Each vane acts as a small low-aspect-ratio wing; its tip vortex transfers momentum toward the wall, raising near-wall velocity. Cost: a small parasite-drag increment.

question: A leading-edge slot delays stall because:

options.text: High-pressure air from below passes through the slot and re-energises the upper boundary layer
It lowers the Reynolds number
It blocks spanwise flow only, which stops the boundary layer from moving toward the tip and so prevents the separation that would otherwise develop near the wing root
It reduces the angle of attack

explanation: The slat/slot gap jet adds momentum at the start of the upper-surface recovery and reduces the suction peak on the main element, so the boundary layer tolerates a higher α.

question: Frost or ice roughness on the upper leading-edge region causes:

options.text: Early transition and separation, reducing CLmax and the stalling angle
Increased CLmax, since turbulent layers resist separation
No change below 10 knots, because at low speed the boundary layer is so thick that surface roughness has no measurable effect on the way the wing separates
Only a drag increase with unchanged stall behaviour

explanation: Roughness at the suction peak thickens the layer and depletes its momentum ahead of the steepest adverse gradient; separation occurs at lower α. Stall can occur before an α-based warning.

question: A stall-warning system triggered at a fixed angle of attack is less protective on a contaminated wing because:

options.text: Contamination has no effect on α at stall
Contamination lowers the stalling angle, possibly below the warning threshold
Contamination raises the stalling angle
The warning depends on airspeed only, so it responds to the speed reading rather than to the actual angle of attack at which the wing is about to stall

explanation: The warning α is set for the clean wing. With a reduced stall α, the wing may stall before or at the same α the warning activates.

question: Wing fences and vortilons on swept wings:

options.text: Increase spanwise flow
Replace the ailerons
Replace the ailerons, since fences and vortilons are fitted in place of the roll controls on any swept wing to take over the job of lateral control
Obstruct or break up spanwise boundary-layer flow toward the tips

explanation: A fence blocks outboard drift; a vortilon sheds a vortex at high α that performs the same function. Both delay tip separation and pitch-up.

question: Heavy rain on the wing surface primarily:

options.text: Roughens the surface film and thickens the boundary layer, reducing CLmax and raising drag
Increases CLmax by adding mass
Has no aerodynamic effect, since the water is shed from the surface within seconds of contact and so never alters the flow over the wing at any point
Reduces drag through lubrication

explanation: Water film and droplet impact act as roughness, promoting early transition and thickening the layer; momentum is also lost accelerating the droplets.
